howto.title: How to read these results
howto.1: Compare each score with the published average beside it. "Above" or "below" shows where this story stands against eight published Sinhala stories, not whether it is good or bad.
howto.2: Fluency and lexical diversity agree best with native readers; coherence agrees moderately.
howto.3: For register, read the highlighted words in the story. A highlighted word may be a slip, a deliberate style choice, or a known false flag, such as the particle ය written as a separate word.
howto.4: The composite is a summary only. Read the four dimensions first.
instr.title: Input instructions
instr.1: Paste one complete short story written in Sinhala script (Unicode). Paste the story text only, without a title, author name or notes.
instr.2: At least 95% of the letters must be Sinhala. A few English words are accepted; romanised Sinhala (Singlish) and other scripts are rejected.
instr.3: Length: SSEF was tested on stories of 488 to 1,273 words. Shorter or longer stories are still scored, but those lengths have not been tested. Maximum 30,000 characters.
instr.4: Put dialogue inside double quotation marks ("…" or “…”), with each speaker's turn in its own paragraph. Text outside quotation marks is treated as narration.
instr.5: SSEF was built and tested on Sinhala love stories. Stories of other genres can be scored, but they have not been tested.
instr.6: Fluency is optional and needs a GPU. It takes about 3 minutes for an 800-word story. The other three scores do not need a GPU.
notice.length: This story has {n} words. SSEF was tested on stories of 488 to 1,273 words, so scores for this length have not been tested.
ttr.label: TTR (baseline, length-sensitive)
register.direction: Higher = narration and dialogue follow the literary/spoken convention more closely. A low narrative score can be a deliberate style, not an error.
note.coherence: Moderate agreement with native-speaker ratings (r = +0.47, n = 30).
note.darc: Validated on controlled register errors (ρ = −0.931) and by a native-speaker reviewer. Matched readers' narration judgement on all 30 stories.
comp.note: Summary only. It did not predict readers' overall-quality ratings (r = +0.25). Read the four dimensions.
story.title: Story — Annotated View
count.line: {n} spoken-register word(s) in narration highlighted; {m} literary-register word(s) in dialogue highlighted. ({k} flagged total)
footer: SSEF gives no good-or-bad verdict and does not measure plot, creativity or enjoyment. Scores are shown against eight published Sinhala stories.
